about: Response shapes of the app routes the playbooks' fakes answer (R1 review fix OR1-pb-6..9, OVN-17), read from each app's code at the commit named. Routes whose OpenAPI response is a concrete model are read from tests/fixtures/openapi/<app>.json instead; an entry here for such a route must name the same top-level fields (tests/contract/test_response_shapes.py). Objects with properties are closed; `required` is what the app always sends.

approval_payload_storage.explanation: Field name is 'payload' (JSONB, exposed verbatim in ApprovalOut.payload). It is built as {<route value-param name>: model_dump(mode='json')} - for POST /detector-sets/send the only value param is 'body', so the agent's request sits NESTED under payload.body as the FULL validated GroupSendRequest dump, defaults filled in: {repositories:{} , namespace:null, visibility:'private', set_ids:[...as sent, duplicates kept]}. The enrich() result is then merged at the TOP level beside 'body' (payload.update): send_group_id (new dsg_ id), sends[{set_id,set_name,send_id (new dsn_ id),approval_digest,versions,registrations}], publish_digests (sorted), repositories (the RESOLVED version_id->repo map, not the request's), registrations (int), visibility (duplicate of body.visibility). Then payload = json.loads(canonical_json(payload)); secret_fields (none for this route; e.g. 'body.access_token' for hf preview/import) are popped and replaced by 'hmac-sha256:<hex>'. request_digest = sha256 hex of canonical_json(stored payload) where canonical_json = json.dumps(sort_keys=True, separators=(',',':'), ensure_ascii=False, allow_nan=False).encode('utf-8'). Consequence: a client CANNOT recompute request_digest from what it sent alone (server-generated ids and plan digests are inside); it can (a) fetch GET /approvals/{id}, recompute sha256(canonical_json(payload)) and compare with request_digest (bare hex) or the 202's 'sha256:'+hex, and (b) compare payload.body with its own request normalised to the model's defaults.

error.message: Approval apr_x is executed; only a pending approval can be approved.

error_envelope.notes: Every error: {'error':{'code','message','details'}}; details is always an object ({} when none). Codes: AppError subclasses use their own (NOT_FOUND, CONFLICT, FORBIDDEN, UNPROCESSABLE, or domain codes such as send_not_found, APPROVAL_NOT_PENDING, AGENT_CANNOT_DECIDE, INVALID_AGENT_IDENTITY). Starlette/FastAPI HTTPException maps status->code (400 BAD_REQUEST, 401 UNAUTHORIZED, 403 FORBIDDEN, 404 NOT_FOUND, 405 METHOD_NOT_ALLOWED, 409 CONFLICT, 413 PAYLOAD_TOO_LARGE, 422 VALIDATION_ERROR, 429 TOO_MANY_REQUESTS, 503 UNAVAILABLE, else HTTP_ERROR) with message = detail (unknown route: 'Not Found'). RequestValidationError -> 422 code VALIDATION_ERROR, message 'The request is not valid.', details {errors:[{loc:[str...],msg,type}]} (or code 'repo_id_invalid' with the field message when that is the only error type). Unhandled -> 500 INTERNAL_ERROR, details {correlation_id}.

details.description: {} when none. 422 VALIDATION_ERROR: {errors:[{loc:[str],msg,type}]}. 500 INTERNAL_ERROR: {correlation_id}. Domain errors put their own keys here (may include 'next').

200.note: Always 200 while the API is up. status 'degraded' only when postgres, redis or data_volume is not ok. millm/mistudio deps (frozen keys) always carry address_source/previous_origins; 'configured'/'url' present per check_http (url absent when not configured); millm gains ui_url when MILLM_UI_URL is set. runner gains contract_version/bundle_digest when it answered JSON. datajuicer_worker.preview_queue only when ok.

All 8 keys always present. verified=true only with reason 'verified against miWorkbench's catalogue' (detail null, definition object, archived bool). Unverified answers: definition/current_version/archived null, detail a sentence, record.source='supplied', record.definition_version/positive_meaning null. Never an error when miWorkbench is absent (200 unverified). Key pattern failure -> 422 VALIDATION_ERROR.

Top-level keys: behaviour_key, counts, objects, shown_per_kind (=20), journey, next, approvals_ahead, complete, note. objects lists at most 20 newest per kind; counts are whole. objects.detector_sends[] items are {id,set_id,state,checks_refused,checks} (counts of checks, not the check list). versions[].census_cells_short is whatever the version's behaviour_census.cells_short holds (often null). next is null exactly when complete is true; next.args is always {behaviour_key}. Read-only, derived; NO 404 for an unknown key.

detail=full (default). state enum is the DB CHECK set SEND_STATES; in practice only queued, running, completed, failed, cancelled are written (send_service docstring: 'no send row exists in awaiting_approval'; nothing writes 'rejected' - a rejected approval leaves NO send, so GET of the approval's payload.sends[].send_id answers 404 send_not_found). checks[] and notes[] items: {code,title,outcome,figure,reason,next_step,source,details}; outcome in green|note|refused; notes = checks with outcome 'note'. run_request is null until every register step has a probe_dataset_id. snapshot/checks/plan are frozen at creation, so snapshot.roles items carry role_out() keys of the creating version (kept open).

202.note: Agent caller (X-Dataworks-Agent: agent:<name>) is ALWAYS gated (no when=; x-approval-when 'always'). Body has exactly approval_id, status ('pending'), action ('hub_push'), request_digest ('sha256:'+hex), expires_at (Python isoformat, '+00:00' suffix), hint. NO summary, NO next (pending_next not set for this route), NO decide_in at this commit. Enrichment (prepare_group: checks, plan, builds) runs BEFORE the approval is stored, so refusals arrive as error envelopes instead of 202: set_not_found 404, send_refused 409 (details.checks), send_in_progress 409, builds_pending 409 (details.builds; builds were started, re-send later), cap_exceeded 422 (details.next), send_group_invalid 422, private_only_public_refused 422, mistudio_not_configured 409; malformed agent header -> 400 INVALID_AGENT_IDENTITY; body problems -> 422 VALIDATION_ERROR (request model is extra=forbid).

200.note: response_model=ApiResponse[list[ModelResponse]] with no exclude_none: every ModelResponse field is always emitted (null when unset). data is a bare list (no total). probe_capacity is filled only by the single-model GET, null in the list. num_parameters/memory_footprint/device/dtype/placement only non-null for the loaded model. lease never carries the lease id.

Query params: armed (bool), behaviour (str<=64), cursor (str<=2048), limit (1..1000, default PROBE_LIST_PAGE_SIZE=200). Envelope is FastAPI response_model serialisation without exclude_none, so success/data/error/meta are ALWAYS emitted (error is null). meta = {next: cursor|null, limit: page size}. Item HAS id ('pr_<12hex>'), name and hf_id. results_total/results_fired/last_result_at are on list (and single GET) items only; last_result_at is a datetime ISO string or null. created_at is a datetime serialised as ISO string. 'load_dtype' is whatever the definition's model.load_dtype says (normally string or null). Invalid cursor -> 400 INVALID_CURSOR in the error envelope.

enum: detects on unseen tasks, compared with a judge

200.note: Query params: probe_id, request_id, session_id(<=24), since, until (ISO 8601), verdict in {fired, not_fired, not_scored}, window(<=16), origin(<=8), behaviour(<=64), score_min, score_max, result_id(<=36), trace_id (32 hex), limit 1..500 default 100, offset (deprecated), cursor, kind in {probe, rule}. With probe_id set, rule results are excluded, so every item is a probe event (kind='probe'). Without probe_id the list is a union of probe events and rule results (kind='rule'). Each item is the legacy keys MERGED with the stored mi.probe.result/v1 object (contract keys win), so many more keys appear (detector_digest, decision, rung_language, completed_at, ...): additionalProperties is true on purpose. Item 'verdict' is a BOOLEAN or null, not the query-string word. No context_text/context_token_ids (only GET /api/probes/events/{id} carries them). meta = {next, limit}.

No query params. data has NO 'catalogue' list: 'catalogue' is counts {imported, behaviours}. 'armed' items DO carry id and paused_reason (paused_reason is the row's, or a synthesised 'no hook is installed ...' sentence for stale rows). There is no hf_id on armed items. windows/threshold/threshold_revision/cost are null when no live hook. budget is a {name: number} map; projected is a map plus over_budget bool. last_retention_pass_at type comes from probe_sessions.counters (timestamp or null), transcripts from settings.PROBE_TRANSCRIPTS (not narrowed here). versions items in behaviours are free-form.

anyOf.description:
Calibrated usable-strength band for the circuit's serving dial (IDL-37).

Badge, not gate. When present, its `[onset, cliff]` is what
`CircuitBudget.intensity_range` is clamped to (a served dial cannot reach
the nonsense zone) and `sweet_spot` is the default `intensity`.

`provisional` is True whenever the probes were GENERATED (not authored) or
the band was measured on the discovery-plane model rather than re-verified
against the served model — an honest confidence marker, never a blocker.

cliff.description: max dial still correct; above this the judge flips to broken
cliff.title: Cliff

onset.description: min dial with influence above baseline noise
onset.title: Onset

items.description:
One falsifiable correctness probe used to find the cliff (IDL-37).

Deliberately a NEUTRAL factual question — a topic the circuit should NOT
influence — so that degradation shows up as the circuit's tint corrupting an
unrelated fact (detectable), rather than as a change to output on the
circuit's own concept (whose "right answer" is not falsifiable). The probe
travels in the contract so a serve-time re-verify is one cheap pass.
items.title: CalibrationProbe

sweet_spot.description: usable dial: strongest still-correct point, with margin
sweet_spot.title: Sweet Spot

items.description:
One SAE the definition references.

`mistudio_sae_id` is the wire name, and `sae_id` is accepted as an input
alias because that is what every other tool in this codebase calls the same
value (`start_circuit_capture` takes `[{layer, sae_id}]`). Pydantic's
default `extra="ignore"` used to turn a caller's `sae_id` into a SILENTLY
NULL `mistudio_sae_id`: the definition validated, persisted and exported
clean, then failed much later at miServer as an unbound SAE, with nothing
pointing back here.

An entry that names no SAE id at all is rejected by `CircuitService`, not
by this model — see the implementation comment below for why the check
cannot live in the schema without publishing a contract that lies.
